a:r.a:t: Humans and Neanderthals Share a Common Ancestor:

p:cNvPr.descr: A syringe-shaped timeline showing the evolutionary history of humans. A syringe-shaped vertical yellow-shaded timeline. The top of the syringe is open. The left side of the syringe is labeled “modern human.” The top right side of the timeline is labeled “Neanderthal”. The left side of the timeline is bracketed and labeled “fossil data”, with dotted lines showing the section of years between 8,000 (top) and 195,000 years ago. At 8,000 years, to the right, is text reading, “Most recent known Neanderthal remains.” Below, at 41,000 years, is text reading, “Earliest modern humans in Europe.” Below this, at 195,000 years, is text reading, “Earliest known anatomically modern humans.” Further down on the timeline is another dashed bracket labeled “genomic data” on the left. The dashed line goes from the bracket over to the right side of the timeline, to 370,000 years ago. Below this there is text reading, “Split of ancestral human and Neanderthal populations.” The dotted line from the bottom of the bracket leads to approximately 706,000 years ago. Below this is text reading, “Coalescence time of human and Neanderthal reference sequences.” Below this is the “tip” of the syringe, which is labeled “evolutionary lineage of human and Neanderthal reference sequences.” To the left of the “tip” is text reading, “Evolutionary lineage of ancestral human and Neanderthal populations.” The timeline then diverges up and to the left, forming a lineage that leads all the way up to the top of the timeline, labeled “modern human.”
